This study urges the need for the regulation of concerned authorities and education programs to help overcome the existing challenges.

Description:
Objective. To compare the energy expenditure of two types of manual wheelchair propulsion.
Design. Experimental and comparative design-using matched controls.
Background. A new manual wheelchair propulsion technique is proposed to minimize the overload exerted on the upper limb during the classical propulsion. The energy cost and other parameters of this new propulsion technique were evaluated.
Methods. Eight paraplegic male adults (Mean±SD) values for age and body mass were 28±4 years and 61.75±8.35 kg and seven able-bodied subjects (age and body mass were respectively 25±2 years and 81.4±7.4 kg) were recruited for this study. Each subject propelled manually two types of wheelchair with two different propulsion techniques. Heart rate and oxygen consumption resulting from each manual propulsion type were calculated and compared.
Results. Mean VO2 peak values were not found to be significantly different between classical and the new proposed wheelchair propulsion for the paraplegic subjects. VO2 values were significantly lower in able-bodied subjects. Maximal Heart Rate were found to be higher when using the classical propulsion technique in both able-bodied and paraplegic groups.
Conclusion. The Classical wheelchair propulsion technique needs to be adapted to the physiological and biomechanical work of the paraplegic’s upper extremities. This study showed the advantage of using a different propulsion technique. More studies are needed to recommend the new technique.

Purpose: This study evaluated the isokinetic muscle strength parameters after 6 months of anterior cruciate ligament rehabilitation in young athletes. Methods: We measured muscle strength of 50 patients, 6 months after surgery after ACL reconstruction. The parameters used to evaluate the strength of the quadriceps and hamstrings were the: peak torque, average power, total work, max repetition total work and the ratio agonist/antagonist (AGO/ANTAG). They were studied at various speeds: 120, 180.300 degrees/sec.

Title: Effectiveness of closed-loop rehabilitation with motor imagery protocol to induce and guide motor recovery in paraplegic patients
Authors: Ahmad RIFAI SARRAJ, Mariam ALZAHER
Description: Neurorehabilitation has been demonstrated as effective to induce and guide histological and/or functional recovery in Spinal Cord Injury (SCI) patients. Evidence from clinical trials, however, recommended that conventional and compensatory rehabilitative strategies, suggested for irremediable sensorimotor deficits using assistive devices should be replaced by restorative strategies. This study aimed is to examine a new experimental rehabilitative protocol of SCI patients, based on the histological and/or functional reorganization model of the spinal cord after injury as well as on the activity-dependent plasticity and motor imagery. Our hypothesis is that a developed closed loop rehabilitation training program, combining specific motor imagery at the higher level and specific sensory inputs at the lower level of spinal injury, can restore voluntary control over paralyzed extremities in incomplete SCI. Results showed significant improvement in frequency and intensity of voluntary attempted movement as well as for sensory and motor exam of the ASIA impairment scale after application of the protocol compared to conventional treatment in control group.

Title: Mise au point Évaluation et approches rééducatives de la spasticité chez les hémiplégiques adultes
Authors: AHMAD RIFAII SARRAJ
Description: La spasticité est connue principalement depuis Charcot en 1863. Les douleurs, les co-contractions, la perte de dextérité, la fatigabilité et autres sont souvent associées à la spasticité et peuvent contribuer largement à l’invalidité. L’évaluation doit être qualitative et/ou quantitative en utilisant plusieurs échelles. Les approches rééducatives sont très diverses et parfois contradictoires, se basant sur le concept de sa neutralisation ou de son inhibition. Cet article présente l’évaluation méthodologique de la spasticité ainsi que les principales approches rééducatives utilisées essentiellement chez les hémiplégiques adultes.
